Developmental delay is typical across the whole GNAO1 spectrum, including the movement-predominant pole, so it is wired from the shared upstream signaling lesion rather than from the epilepsy endpoint; the intervening neurodevelopmental mechanism is not established.
Intellectual disability of variable severity is likewise characteristic of both poles, and is attributed to the shared disruption of Gao-dependent neurodevelopment rather than to seizures alone.
Axial hypotonia, common early in life across the spectrum, follows from the shared signaling lesion through intermediates that have not been resolved.
Dysregulated cortical neurotransmitter release shifts the excitation-inhibition balance.

edges.description: Loss-of-function alleles (reduced cAMP inhibition) contribute to the cortical network imbalance of the epilepsy pole.
Gain-of-function alleles (enhanced cAMP inhibition) segregate toward the movement pole, linking this arm to basal-ganglia output dysregulation.
Cortical hyperexcitability generates seizures and drives the encephalopathy.
Dysregulated basal-ganglia output produces the hyperkinetic movement disorder.
The epilepsy-pole endpoint is observed clinically as a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with infantile-onset, often drug-resistant seizures.
In a subset the seizures take the form of epileptic spasms, including an Ohtahara-syndrome / early infantile DEE presentation.
Focal-onset seizures predominate in the later-onset epilepsy cluster.
Generalized-onset seizures, including tonic-clonic, occur particularly in the later-onset, more drug-responsive cluster.
Seizures in the epilepsy-predominant pole can escalate to status epilepticus.
Chorea is a hallmark expression of the hyperkinetic movement disorder.
Dystonia is the other hallmark expression, frequently mixed with chorea and prone to severe exacerbations.
The mixed choreoathetotic pattern affecting the whole body is the characteristic combined form of the hyperkinetic movement disorder.

Feeding difficulties worsen during hyperkinetic crises. The baseline contribution of global neurological impairment is not separated from the movement-disorder contribution in the sources, so the edge is marked indirect with unresolved intermediates.

nodes.description: Seizures are treated with antiseizure medications. Seizures in the epilepsy-predominant DEE pole are frequently drug-resistant, whereas the later-onset epilepsy cluster is often infrequent or well controlled with standard antiseizure medications.

evidence.snippet: Five patients had well-controlled epilepsy and 1 had drug-resistant seizures

nodes.description: Disrupted Go signaling in striatal medium spiny neurons (which express Gao and its coupled D2 dopamine and other receptors) dysregulates basal-ganglia motor output. This node captures the single concept of the movement-disorder effector arm, kept separate from the cortical/epilepsy arm.
Chorea is a hallmark of the movement-predominant pole, often as part of a mixed hyperkinetic dyskinesia.

evidence.snippet: Movement disorders are characterized by dystonia and choreoathetosis

nodes.description: A mixed choreoathetotic movement pattern affecting the whole body is common in the movement-predominant pole.

Disrupted inhibitory G-protein signaling shifts the balance of excitation and inhibition in cortical networks toward hyperexcitability. This node captures the single concept of the cortical network imbalance and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.
Globus pallidus internus (GPi) deep brain stimulation is used for the severe, medically refractory hyperkinetic movement disorder and can be life-saving in status dystonicus / hyperkinetic crisis.

evidence.snippet: Emergency deep brain stimulation (DBS) was life saving in 1 patient, resulting in immediate clinical benefit with complete cessation of violent hyperkinetic movements
Deep brain stimulation should be considered early in the treatment of refractory or prolonged dyskinetic crisis

nodes.description: The clinical result of the cortical arm is early-onset, often multiple-type and drug-resistant seizures with developmental impairment - a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. This node captures the single concept of the epilepsy-pole endpoint and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.

evidence.snippet: in four individuals with epileptic encephalopathy

nodes.description: As a Gi/o-family subunit, Gao contributes to modulation of adenylyl cyclase-cAMP signaling downstream of inhibitory GPCRs; variants perturb this control in either direction. In vitro cAMP-inhibition assays classify GNAO1 variants by their effect on this arm - loss-of-function (reduced cAMP inhibition) segregates toward the epilepsy pole, whereas gain-of-function (enhanced cAMP inhibition) segregates toward the movement pole. This node captures the single concept of the second-messenger effector arm, which feeds both output poles.

loss-of-function (LOF) GNAO1 alleles cause epilepsy and gain-of-function (GOF) alleles are primarily associated with movement disorders

evidence.snippet: we identified de novo heterozygous mutations in GNAO1, which encodes a Gαo subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, in four individuals with epileptic encephalopathy

The GNAO1 LOF mutations are associated with epileptic encephalopathy while GOF mutants (such as G42R, G203R, and E246K) or normally functioning mutants (R209) were found in patients with movement disorders with or without seizures

nodes.description: A de novo heterozygous variant in GNAO1 alters Gao, the alpha subunit of the Go heterotrimeric G protein. This node captures the single concept of the initiating genetic lesion; most variants are missense changes clustering in the GTPase/nucleotide-binding and switch regions of the protein.
Generalized-onset (including tonic-clonic) seizures occur, particularly in the later-onset, more drug-responsive epilepsy cluster.
Global developmental delay is typical across the spectrum and is often severe in the DEE pole.

The clinical result of the basal-ganglia arm is a hyperkinetic movement disorder - chorea, dystonia, or a mixed dyskinesia affecting the whole body, with a tendency to spontaneous or triggered exacerbations and potentially life-threatening hyperkinetic crises (status dystonicus). This node captures the single concept of the movement-pole endpoint.

evidence.snippet: severe motor and cognitive impairment with marked choreoathetosis, self-injurious behavior, and epileptic encephalopathy

nodes.description: Axial hypotonia is common, particularly early in life.

Normally the Gbg subunit released from activated Go inhibits presynaptic voltage-gated (Cav2.1/Cav2.2) calcium channels to restrain neurotransmitter release and activates GIRK potassium channels. Variant Go disrupts this Gbg-mediated brake, dysregulating synaptic neurotransmitter release. This node captures the single concept of the synaptic/ion-channel effector arm and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.

nodes.description: The variant Gao subunit disrupts the Go signaling cycle - abnormal guanine nucleotide binding/hydrolysis, reduced or altered coupling to inhibitory G-protein-coupled receptors, and in some variants a dominant-negative effect on wild-type Gao. This node captures the single concept of the shared upstream molecular lesion, from which two distinct effector arms diverge.

evidence.snippet: GNAO1 encodes Gαo, the α subunit of Go, a member of the Gi/o family of heterotrimeric G protein signal transducers. Go is the most abundant membrane protein in the mammalian central nervous system and plays major roles in synaptic neurotransmission and neurodevelopment
These data suggest that aberrant Gαo signaling can cause multiple neurodevelopmental phenotypes, including epileptic encephalopathy and involuntary movements

The vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) inhibitor tetrabenazine is used to suppress the hyperkinetic movement disorder (chorea/dyskinesia), including in the management of hyperkinetic exacerbations.

evidence.snippet: tetrabenazine was effective in partially controlling dyskinesia for 2/7 patients
